summary: Five inactive proofs construct Sobolev-capacity control of bounded admissible first-Hessian coefficients, canonical quasicontinuity for countable families, weighted linear-current convergence, and symmetry/simultaneous decreasing convergence for D2 and shifted Q2. The proof uses a conformal Gauduchon trace with its nonclosed first-order drift retained. Higher-degree products are not covered.
scoped_mathematical_obligations: T is rho times omega^(n-1), not an arbitrary Gauduchon test; this conformal choice makes the first-cone trace positive.
T is smooth strictly positive and ddc-closed, giving a fixed positive trace mass A and a genuine norm equivalent to H1.
The capacity is first defined using H1 functions constrained almost everywhere on OPEN sets and then outer open supersets; no dense-set smooth constraint or unproved countable subadditivity is used.
Truncation to[0,1] and the Sobolev maximum chain rule bound the squared norm of finite maxima by the sum; summable excess errors pass to the countable union.
The level-set test min(1,|f|/a) gives a^-2 times the squared H1 norm.

Positive chart mollification with a partition of unity preserves value1 on any fixed compact subset of an open constrained set; H1 convergence yields the Radon-measure bound without already assuming quasicontinuity.
The exact smooth energy identity is integral du wedge dc u wedge T=-integral u ddc u wedge T, with ddc(u^2) contributing the factor2.
Positive trace and equal mass A bound that energy by2MA; bounded approximants have a common M+1 bound after a finite initial segment.
Strong L2 convergence and weak H1 compactness identify every cluster point with the canonical limit almost everywhere, giving whole-sequence weak H1 convergence.
The first-order Stokes identity retains the exact plus integral phi dc u wedge dT drift; dT is not presumed zero.
Trace is an H1-dual positive Radon measure, so its Borel-set mass is bounded by the square root of Sobolev capacity.
The closed Gamma2 inequality controls every first-Hessian coefficient by the nonnegative omega trace; the restriction m>=2 is essential.
Coefficient domination passes from independent smooth approximants to the canonical current, and the smooth-volume term is absorbed using volume<=capacity<=norm(1)^2.
Mazur combinations use tails j>=N, ensuring u<=w_N<=u_N pointwise; the resulting continuous-outside-small-sets function is the specified canonical potential.
The geometric8^-N H1 errors and2^-N thresholds give a summable16^-N capacity tail, with uniformly summable pointwise differences on its complement.
A countable family has a common open exceptional set by allocating a summable capacity budget.
Distributional first-Hessian convergence plus uniform coefficient variations gives weak signed-measure convergence against continuous compactly supported tests.
Common quasicontinuity and pointwise decreasing convergence permit Dini on the compact complement; Tietze gives a bounded continuous comparison weight.
Both varying and limiting coefficient measures obey the same capacity bound; the weighted pairing error tends to zero by first taking the sequence limit and then the capacity budget to zero.
Weighted convergence permits ddc of v_j ddc u_j; smooth simultaneous products are symmetric, identifying D2 in both orderings.
The existing subset expansion and uniform positive-current mass bound give weak Q2 convergence; its degree is top only when m=2.
Unwedged D2 has order zero only in the stated m>2 regime inherited from the earlier coefficient bounds; no new m=2 unwedged measure assertion is made.
No capacity domination for products of two first Hessians, higher-degree interchange, general bounded regularity or Hessian comparison is inferred.
